_comment: Curated clinically-significant drug interaction rules for hospice care. Rules match by drug CLASS pair (preferred, broad coverage) or by exact drug-name pair (specific, high-value pairs). Open/curated dataset intended to be swapped for a licensed feed (First Databank / Medi-Span) later without changing callers.
_hospice_note: Opioid + benzodiazepine is intentionally NOT flagged as a class-pair interaction: this combination is a standard, physician-ordered comfort-kit pairing for end-of-life symptom management (dyspnea, terminal agitation) in hospice care, not an incidental/erroneous combination. Flagging it here would create false-positive alert fatigue for the most common hospice comfort regimen.

class_pairs.management: Monitor sedation level and respiratory rate; avoid stacking additional sedating agents.
Monitor sedation/respiratory rate closely; consider dose reduction.

class_pairs.effect: Additive CNS/respiratory depression, increased fall risk
class_pairs.management: Monitor sedation, respiratory status, and fall risk; consider dose reduction.
Monitor sedation level and fall risk.

class_pairs.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome (can be life-threatening)
class_pairs.management: Avoid combination; requires washout period between agents per prescriber guidance.
Avoid combination; contact prescriber immediately.

class_pairs.effect: Increased serotonergic burden / serotonin syndrome risk
class_pairs.management: Monitor for agitation, tremor, hyperthermia, diaphoresis.
Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms; use lowest effective doses.
Avoid combination when possible; monitor for bleeding, consider GI protection.
Combination sometimes clinically necessary (e.g., cardiac); monitor closely for bleeding.
Monitor for bleeding; consider GI protection.

class_pairs.effect: Increased bleeding risk (SSRIs impair platelet function)
class_pairs.management: Monitor for bruising/bleeding.
Monitor potassium and renal function.
Monitor serum potassium.
Monitor potassium and renal function.

class_pairs.effect: Increased risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment
class_pairs.management: Dual RAAS blockade generally avoided; confirm with prescriber.

class_pairs.effect: Diuretic-induced hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity risk
class_pairs.management: Monitor potassium and digoxin levels; watch for toxicity signs (nausea, visual changes, arrhythmia).

class_pairs.effect: Diuretic-induced hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity risk
class_pairs.management: Monitor potassium and digoxin levels.

class_pairs.effect: Additive bradycardia and AV nodal blockade
class_pairs.management: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure.
Monitor digoxin level and heart rate.
Digoxin dose typically reduced ~50%; monitor levels closely.
Consider ECG monitoring if clinically appropriate; avoid stacking multiple QT-prolonging agents.

class_pairs.effect: Additive anticholinergic burden (confusion, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, falls)
class_pairs.management: Review necessity of each agent; consider deprescribing per anticholinergic burden guidance.
Monitor INR closely if on warfarin.

class_pairs.effect: Increased statin levels / myopathy-rhabdomyolysis risk (CYP3A4 inhibition)
class_pairs.management: Consider holding statin during macrolide course, or use azithromycin (less CYP3A4 effect).

class_pairs.effect: Increased statin levels / myopathy risk (CYP3A4 inhibition)
class_pairs.management: Consider dose reduction or temporary hold of statin.
Monitor sedation; consider dose adjustment.
Monitor INR closely with warfarin; dose adjustment often needed.

class_pairs.effect: Significantly increased anticoagulant effect / bleeding risk
class_pairs.management: Monitor INR closely; anticipate warfarin dose reduction.
Monitor for GI symptoms; consider GI protection.
Monitor lithium levels closely.
Monitor lithium levels closely.
Monitor lithium levels.
Monitor lithium levels and renal function.
Monitor blood glucose closely.
Monitor blood glucose more closely; educate on non-adrenergic hypoglycemia signs.
Review necessity; monitor for confusion, constipation, urinary retention.
Review necessity of each agent; monitor for confusion, constipation, urinary retention.
Consider ECG monitoring if clinically indicated.

drug_pairs.effect: Additive QT prolongation risk with methadone
drug_pairs.management: Avoid combination if possible; ECG monitoring recommended.
Monitor INR closely; anticipate warfarin dose reduction.
Monitor INR closely; warfarin dose typically reduced.
